MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JANUARY 23, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:04 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR HUFF.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Mayor Huff led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Serviced Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  Following staff’s response to an inquiry from Councilmember Zuckerman regarding the
  investment report and from Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell regarding the Park & Activities
  Commission minutes:

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-J AS RECOMMENDED.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  AND 59310 THROUGH 59404 IN THE AMOUNT OF $644,022.16 FOR A GRAND

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JANUARY 23, 2018
 6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  Harbor Sight residents Glenn Komae, Vince Vassallo and Bob Bennett addressed the
  Council to request the City’s assistance in challenging a Rancho Palos Verdes land use
  decision regarding a project at 27581 Palos Verdes Drive East and appealing the recent
  permit approval which affects several Harbor Sight residents.

  Following brief discussion, the COUNCIL concurred in providing the following direction to
  staff:

  PREPARE A LETTER FOR THE MAYOR’S SIGNATURE REQUESTING THAT THE
  RANCHO PALOS VERDES CITY COUNCIL TAKE THE HARBOR SIGHT
  RESIDENTS CONCERNS INTO ACCOUNT WHEN MAKING ITS DECISION
  REGARDING THE PROJECT AT 27581 PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER AT 7:30 P.M. AS NOTICED)

A.  RESOLUTION 2414 APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE OF 2018-19 COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) receive any
  public testimony; 3) close the Public Hearing; 4) waive further reading and approve
  Resolution No. 2414 authorizing the execution of a contract with the Los Angeles County
  Community Development Commission for participation in the program for funding of
  the ADA Access Ramp and Sidewalk Improvement Program as identified in the Programs
  and Conditions Assessment Report dated April 2, 2014 in the amount of approximately
  $21,876.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED AND CALLED FOR

  There was no public comment.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 23, 2018
   MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2414 AUTHORIZING THE
  EXECUTION OF A CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM FOR
  FUNDING OF THE ADA ACCESS RAMP AND SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM AS IDENTIFIED IN THE PROGRAMS AND CONDITIONS
  ASSESSMENT REPORT DATED APRIL 2, 2014 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  APPROXIMATELY $21,876.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2414 by title only.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the items listed and make any additions
  or deletions.

  City Manager Prichard presented the staff report listing the proposed items for
  discussion at the Policy Development Session scheduled for Tuesday, March 14, 2018
  beginning at 4:00 p.m.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that he will be on call for jury duty the week of
  March 13, 2018 so his available for a 4:00 p.m. start is questionable at this time.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL’S suggestion that the City consider hosting
  a shred day for residents, Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that the city currently
  offers a document shredding event in conjunction with the City’s Earth Day celebration
  at the Promenade on the Peninsula. Following brief discussion, it was suggested that
  staff look into possibly offering a second event and further promoting the existing
  document shredding event.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL suggested that a discussion regarding stormwater costs
  and regulations be added to the Policy Development Session.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that a general discussion regarding public
  transit be added to the Policy Development Session given the current issues facing PV
  Transit.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT AS AMENDED TO
  ADD THE TWO ITEMS SUGGESTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 23, 2018
 B.  JUNE 5, 2018 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION RESOLUTIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and adopt the following resolutions: 1)
  Resolution No. 2411 – Calling for the holding of a General Municipal Election to be held
  in the City of Rolling Hills Estates on June 5, 2018; 2) Resolution No. 2412 – Requesting
  the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors consolidate said election with the
  Statewide Direct Primary Election; and 3) Resolution No. 2413 – Adopting regulations
  pertaining to candidate statements.

  City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2411 CALLING FOR THE
  HOLDING OF A GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD IN THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ON JUNE 5, 2018.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2411 by title only.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 2412 REQUESTING THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS CONSOLIDATE SAID ELECTION
  WITH THE STATEWIDE DIRECT PRIMARY ELECTION AS AMENDED TO
  CORRECT THE TYPOGRAPHICAL ERROR ON PAGE

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2412 by title only.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2413 ADOPTING
  REGULATIONS PERTAINING TO CANDIDATE STATEMENTS.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding the cost for translation of
  candidate statements, City Clerk Luce explained that the County will be translating the
  statements into the required languages, but the candidates will not be required to pay
  the individual cost of translation but rather just the proportionate share of the space

  Hearing no further comments, MAYOR HUFF called for a roll call vote.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2413 by title only.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 23, 2018
 C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF DECEMBER
  18, 2017 – PROPOSED POCKET PARK DESIGN TASKS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to enter into an agreement with

  donation to the Rolling Hills Pepper Tree Foundation in the amount required to cover

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
JANUARY 23, 2018
 9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSED AMENDED BUSINESS LICENSE TAX ORDINANCE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) approve the proposed ordinance as to form
  and 2) direct staff to prepare a resolution placing the proposed ordinance on the June
  5, 2018 ballot.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material) noting
  that correspondence that was received on this matter since the agenda was published
  has been placed on the dais.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  commented that it has been at least 30 years since the City last increased business
  license tax rates.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that an update to the Business License Tax
  is long overdue and the City’s object is to create balance with the revised ordinance. City
  Manager Prichard commented that in addition to adjusting the rates, the amended
  ordinance also simplifies and streamlines the licensing process and eliminates some
  fees.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she and MAYOR HUFF met with
  Chamber representatives to discuss the proposed ordinance where there was discussion
  about the tax for professionals and that may be an item for discussion this evening
  along with the concern raised in the letter from Bill Pettit sent on behalf of Merrell
  Gardens.

  MAYOR HUFF noted that the letter from Peninsula Seniors also raised the same concern
  regarding the rates for senior living facilities as the letter from Merrell Gardens.

  Tim Buresh, resident and business owner addressed the City Council to express concern
  regarding some of changes in the proposed amended business license tax ordinance as
  currently drafted. He suggested implementing compliance and enforcement
  mechanisms; allowing for online processing; keeping the tax structure competitive with
  surrounding communities and commented that now is not a good time for a tax increase
  given the other competing issues. He further suggested using flat rates rather than gross
  receipts in determining the tax rate and reducing rate for senior living facilities and
  professional services.

  Eileen Hupp, President and CEO, Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber addressed the City
  Council on behalf of the Chamber Board of Directors to express concern regarding the
  proposed amended business license tax ordinance as currently drafted. She stated that
  the board is opposed to the ordinance as drafted and suggests several items for
  consideration including: not using gross receipts to calculate rates and maintaining a
  completive edge by keep rates below neighboring cities. She further expressed the
  Board’s concern regarding the proposed rates for professional services, commercial and
  rental properties and residential care facilities; and suggested that the process provide
  for online processing and specify that non-profits are exempt. She further reiterated
